question: What validation contract should govern prompt-bearing Markdown from local workspaces, installed skills, and ClawHub: advisory findings, install-time blocking, runtime blocking, or source-specific trust policies?
rationale: The issue spans multiple owners and changes how existing user-authored workspace files and installed skills may be accepted at runtime; source inspection shows no current shared contract from which a safe enforcement default can be inferred.

options.title: Design a shared source-aware policy
options.body: Define trust classes, rules, severity, operator override, diagnostics, upgrade behavior, and the owner boundary before implementation.

options.title: Limit to advisory install scanning
options.body: Add non-blocking findings to skill installation and publishing first, leaving runtime workspace ingestion unchanged until the threat model is validated.

options.title: Defer core enforcement to external scanning
options.body: Document an external scanner workflow and revisit core policy only if a missing plugin or install-time API is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Design a shared source-aware policy
recommendation.body: Define trust classes, rules, severity, operator override, diagnostics, upgrade behavior, and the owner boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing maintainer discussion already scoped the unresolved security boundary across the relevant core paths.
